libraries.group: Imported for you, in every program
The Java types the standard library rests on

modules.brief: Read, write, edit and list the files of the workspace.
modules.detail:
Reading is the cheap direction of this sandbox and writing is the expensive one, so a program that reads a dozen files to decide what to change is well shaped, while one that rewrites forty large files in a single turn will exhaust its fuel budget.

Nothing here places anything in the agent's context window. `gg.views.openFile` is the call that does.

modules.brief: Run shell commands in the workspace.
modules.detail:
One function, and the way a program reaches everything gg has no tool for: a build, a test run, `git`, `curl`, a package manager. The workspace is the working directory.

A non-zero exit is a result rather than a failure, because deciding whether a build or a test run passed is the single most common thing a program does with one.

modules.brief: The epic and issue board, shared by every agent in the run.
modules.detail:
An issue is the heavyweight unit of work: its scope, non-scope and completion criteria are exactly what a delegated child agent is briefed from, which is why creating one asks for more than adding a task does. Its five required parts are positional, and the four a program may say nothing about are default arguments, so a call that wants one of them names that one and no other.

Two of a revision's fields are three-way, and `gg.core.Patch` is how all three states are said.

modules.brief: The agent's own task list, which is a directed acyclic graph rather than a list of lines.
modules.detail:
A task is the lightweight unit of work: an id chosen by the caller, a title, and the tasks that must be done first. Nothing dispatches a task and nothing reviews one, which is what separates it from an issue on the board.

A revision's description is three-way, and `gg.core.Patch` says all three states without a sentinel: leaving the argument out keeps what is there, `Patch.Clear` empties it, and `Patch.Replace` replaces it.

modules.brief: Durable notes that survive a context compaction.
modules.detail:
A run picks one of three memory strategies and binds only that strategy's functions, so what this module offers is the honest answer to what memory can do here. The scratchpad keeps every memory in the context window; the two file-shaped strategies keep the contents outside it, one behind an index that is always in context and one behind a keyword search. Deleting is bound under all three.

Every mutation hands back the budget after it, so a program decides whether to write another memory by reading numbers rather than by parsing a sentence about them.

modules.brief: The only way material enters the agent's own context window.
modules.detail:
Under responses as code a whole program's output would otherwise collapse into one anonymous blob of logs, charged to one band, attributable to nothing and closable by nothing. A view restores what tool calling gave for free: one message per view, carrying the band it is charged to and the selector it can be closed by.

So `println` reaches the run's operator and a view reaches the model, which is the whole reason a program that computes something also has to show it.

modules.brief: Managing the agent's own context window.
modules.detail: These are the only calls whose effect is on the conversation rather than on the workspace, and they are worth making from a program precisely because a program can decide when to: read a set of files, extract what matters, then evict the views in the same turn.

modules.brief: Handing scoped work to child agents, and handing this session on to another agent.
modules.detail:
Waiting for children can dominate a turn's wall clock — it blocks while real agents run — and the run's budget keeps ticking while it does, so a program does better to spawn broadly and wait once than to spawn and wait in a loop.

The brief is where this arm's types earn their keep: a child is briefed either with a self-contained prompt or with a board issue, and because that choice is a sealed type rather than two optional arguments, "both" and "neither" are programs that do not compile.

modules.brief: The authored skill library, read by name.
modules.detail: A skill name is a plain `String` rather than an enum entry, because the catalogue is per run while this SDK is compiled once. The system prompt lists the names available, and an unknown one comes back as a failure carrying the full list.

modules.brief: The library of programs this agent has already run.
modules.detail:
Under responses as code a reply is a whole program, so a one-character mistake in a sixty-line program costs the sixty lines again. The library makes the fix proportional to the mistake: fetch what ran, patch it with ordinary string work, hand it back.

```
gg.programs.rerun(gg.programs.get().replace("gg.files.readfile", "gg.files.readFile"))
```

modules.brief: Ending the session, in the shape the agent's own role calls for.
modules.detail:
Under responses as code every reply is a program, so there is no prose turn that could mean "the work is done" — a model that answers "task complete" has written a reply that failed to be a program rather than an ending. These are the calls that mean it.

Which of them a program gets is decided by the agent's role: one that does work is given the plain ending, and one that reviews is given the verdict pair instead. No agent holds both, because an ending is a result and the two roles produce different results.

modules.brief: The failure type, the failure codes, and the small values every other module speaks in.
modules.detail: It catalogues no capability of its own. What it holds is the vocabulary the other eleven modules share, gathered here so that no module has to reach into another to name a failure — and so that a program catching one writes a single `import gg.core.ToolError` rather than one per module it calls. The session-wide `lib` namespace sits here for the same reason: a code module arrives from a skill or from a memory, so it belongs to neither.

functions.name: readFile
functions.brief: Read a file, as either a `gg.files.TextFile` or an `gg.files.ImageFile`.
functions.detail:
Which of the two comes back is detected from the file's bytes rather than from the extension, so a mislabelled picture is still a picture. `gg.files.FileRead` is sealed, so a `when` over the two arms needs no `else`:

```
when (val read = gg.files.readFile("logo.png")) {
    is gg.files.TextFile -> gg.views.openText("logo", read.contents)
    is gg.files.ImageFile -> gg.views.openText("logo", read.label)
}
```

A relative path resolves against the workspace; an absolute one is read as given, so anything else in this container — an offloaded command's output under `/tmp/gg-shell`, say — is readable. This call hands bytes to the program and places nothing in the context window, and reading a picture describes it without showing it, so a file only read here is a file nobody has looked at.

The window is honoured only under a capped read policy; where it is not, the whole file comes back and `gg.files.TextFile.totalLines` says how much of it was returned.

Returns: the file's text, or the picture's description

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND` for a missing path.

functions.name: run
functions.brief: Run a command with `sh -c` in the workspace and hand back its merged output.
functions.detail:
A non-zero exit is not a failure: `gg.shell.ShellOutput.exitCode` carries it. Only a process that could not be launched, or one the timeout killed, raises.

This run may offload shell output, and the `shell` tool's own description says which mode is in force. Under `offload`, `gg.shell.ShellOutput.output` holds only the tail that fits and ends with a note naming the two files the command's full standard output and standard error were written to. Under `adaptive`, the default, a command that succeeded returns no output at all beyond that note, and one that failed returns the tail. Grepping the named files is cheaper than running the command again.

Returns: what the command printed, and how it exited

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` when the timeout killed the process, and `IO_ERROR` when it could not be launched.

functions.name: openFile
functions.brief: Read a file and show it: the read's own answer comes back, and the file becomes its own view.
functions.detail:
The split from `gg.files.readFile` is the point — that call gets bytes for the program, this one shows a file to the model — so a program that reads forty files to grep them still places nothing in the window. An image file is shown as a picture, and this is the only way to look at one.

Naming a window shows one page rather than the whole file. Two pages of one file are two views that coexist; re-opening the same page replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate.

Returns: the file's text, or the picture's description

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND` for a missing path, and `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an offset past the end of the file. The read is what fails, and nothing is opened when it does.

Closing a file view forgets what was read rather than what exists; closing a text view discards the only copy of what it held.

Returns: how many views were closed

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an empty selector.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.doc: What the view is filed under: a file's path, a text view's label, or a documentation view's function name.

functions.name: current
functions.brief: List what is open in the context window right now.
functions.detail:
Each view carries its `gg.views.OpenView.kind`, the `gg.views.OpenView.selector` that closes it, roughly what it costs in `gg.views.OpenView.tokens`, and — for a paged file view — the `gg.views.OpenView.region` it covers. It is what a program reads before deciding what to close when the window is filling up.

Returns: every view open in the context window

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `UNAVAILABLE` when this run bound no view functions at all.

functions.name: evictFileView
functions.brief: Drop the contents of files that were read out of the context window, and report what that reclaimed.
functions.detail:
The files on disk are untouched: this forgets what was read, not what exists.

Returns: what the eviction reclaimed

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND` when the named path has no view open.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file whose views to drop. Left out, every file that was read is dropped.

functions.name: archiveThread
functions.brief: Move whole turns out of the context window and report what that reclaimed.
functions.detail:
Every result carries a header with its turn number and roughly what holding it costs, so the turns worth dropping are named as ranges — which is what a span of integers is in this language. `gg.context.archiveThread(4..19)` archives turns 4 through 19, and `4..<20` means the same span. The agent's own messages in an archived turn are dropped; the results are kept and stay searchable.

Returns: what the archive reclaimed

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a span whose ends are not turn numbers.

parameters.name: ranges
parameters.doc: The spans of turn numbers to move out of the window.

functions.name: searchArchive
functions.brief: Search archived history for a case-insensitive substring, most recent first, up to 8 hits.
functions.detail:
`gg.context.ArchiveSearch.archiveEmpty` is worth reading before the hits: it distinguishes "nothing has been archived yet" from "the search ran and matched nothing", so a program does not archive again believing the first archive failed.

Returns: what the search found, and whether there was anything to search

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an empty query.

parameters.name: query
parameters.doc: The substring to look for. Matching is case-insensitive.

functions.name: compact
functions.brief: Compact the context window: the detailed thread is dropped and restarted from a summary.
functions.detail:
The skills, memories and task list are kept as they are. gg asks for this call when the window is full, and every other call is refused until it is made.

It does not stop the program: it registers the request and returns, and the rewrite happens once the program has ended. Everything not in the summary and not named in `files` is gone, so the summary is written for the agent that resumes and the file list is what it will need in hand.

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `REFUSED` when a compaction is already in flight and this call is not the one it asked for.

signatures.signature: compact(summary: String, vararg files: String): Unit

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: What the restarted window opens with, written for the agent that resumes.

parameters.name: files
parameters.doc: The paths to read afresh into the restarted window. Naming none reads nothing back.

functions.name: spawnSubagent
functions.brief: Delegate scoped work to a child agent and hand back its handle immediately.
functions.detail:
The child runs in parallel while the program continues. The agent named is one of those this agent may spawn — the system prompt lists them — and it selects the child's model, tools and instructions. The child shares this workspace.

Returns: the child's handle, to wait on or to message

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` at the delegation depth cap, and `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an agent this one may not spawn.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent profile to run the child as, from the ones this agent may spawn.

parameters.name: brief
parameters.doc: What the child is to do: `Brief.Prompt` with self-contained instructions, or `Brief.Issue` with the id of a board issue to brief it from.

functions.name: waitForSubagents
functions.brief: Block until the named children have finished, and collect their results in dispatch order.
functions.detail:
Naming none waits for every child still outstanding. The run's wall-clock budget keeps running while the wait does, so one wait for many children costs less than one wait per child.

Returns: every collected child's result, in dispatch order

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.doc: The children to wait for, as spawning returned them. Naming none waits for every one still outstanding.

functions.name: sendMessage
functions.brief: Deliver a message to a running child agent's inbox, which it reads at its next turn.
functions.detail: Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND` for an unknown agent id, and `CONFLICT` when that child has already returned.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.doc: The child to deliver to, as spawning returned it.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to put in its inbox.

functions.name: transitionState
functions.brief: Move the state machine driving this session on to another of its states.
functions.detail:
The state is named the way an agent to spawn is named. It is bound only when a state machine is driving the session and the current state has somewhere to go.

Like compaction it is registered rather than performed: the call validates the target, returns, and the program runs on to its end — the transition happens after that, because replacing the agent and its window mid-program would pull every remaining call out from under it. The first declaration in a turn stands.

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a state this session may not move to, and `REFUSED` for a second declaration in one turn.

signatures.signature: transitionState(state: String, note: String? = null): Unit

parameters.name: state
parameters.doc: The state to move on to, named the way an agent to spawn is named.

parameters.name: note
parameters.doc: The opening message the next state's agent sees. Left out, it sees nothing.

functions.name: exec
functions.brief: Continue this session as a different agent, from the next turn on.
functions.detail:
The named agent takes over with its own model, tools and instructions, keeping every capability the two of them both have — the whole conversation above all, so it needs no catching up.

Registered rather than performed, exactly as a state transition is and for the same reason: the window would otherwise be pulled out from under the program still composing into it. A session makes one succession per turn. It is bound only when this agent may make agent transitions and has agents it may become, and never while a state machine is driving the session.

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an agent this one may not become, and `REFUSED` for a second succession in one turn.

signatures.signature: exec(agent: String, prompt: String? = null): Unit

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to become, from the ones this agent may become.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: The opening message for it. It already holds the whole conversation, so this is the instruction rather than a briefing. Left out, it is given nothing.

functions.name: fork
functions.brief: Run a copy of this agent, in parallel, on something it will not do itself.
functions.detail:
The copy has the same model, the same tools and a private copy of the whole conversation, so the prompt is the difference rather than a briefing: everything already worked out is already there.

Its handle comes back immediately, but the copy itself starts once this turn's tool results are recorded, because the conversation it inherits has to be a complete one. So a wait can only collect it on a later turn, and waiting on it in the program that made it never returns anything.

Returns: the copy's handle, to collect on a later turn

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` at the delegation depth cap.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: What the copy is to do instead. It holds the whole conversation already, so this is the difference rather than a briefing.

functions.name: readSkill
functions.brief: Read a skill by name, which also pins its body permanently into the context window.
functions.detail:
The body comes back with its front matter stripped, and a skill that has been read stays read.

A skill may be code rather than prose, or as well as it. Code is bound at `lib.<key>` for the rest of the session and the reply names the key and what it exports, reachable through `gg.core.lib`. An on-use script runs once the program has ended, and whatever it shows arrives on the next turn.

Returns: the skill's body, with its front matter stripped

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND`, listing the skills that do exist, when the name is unknown.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The skill's name, as the system prompt lists it.

functions.name: history
functions.brief: The programs this session has already run, oldest first.
functions.detail:
Each carries the turn it ran on, how big it was, and whether it ran to its end. It lists shapes rather than sources, so fetching one is a separate call: a directory that inlined every program would put the whole session back in front of the model, which is the one thing the library exists to avoid.

The list survives a compaction, so it is also how a program whose text has left the context window is found again. A session that has run nothing yet gets an empty list rather than a failure.

Returns: every program this session has run, oldest first

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `UNAVAILABLE` when this agent keeps no program library.

functions.name: get
functions.brief: The exact source of one program that ran, as a string.
functions.detail:
This is the first half of fixing a program without rewriting it: get what ran, patch it with ordinary string work, and hand the result back to be run. What comes back is the program that executed — so when a turn's program was itself handed over, the answer is the program that ran rather than the few lines that asked for it, and fetch, patch and run compose turn after turn.

Returns: the source of the program that ran on that turn

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND`, naming the turns that are held, for a turn that ran no program or one the library has dropped.

parameters.name: turn
parameters.doc: The turn whose program to fetch, as the history reports it. Left out, the most recent program comes back.

functions.name: rerun
functions.brief: Hand gg a program to run in place of this one.
functions.detail:
The current program finishes, then gg compiles and runs `source` as this turn's program. Nothing is undone: every call already made stands, and the program that runs next sees the world this one left behind, so a hand-over comes before work that should not be done twice.

The first call stands, because a silently replaced program is a change nobody can see. A program that then fails cancels the hand-over along with everything else it decided, and the turn ends as an ordinary error. Chains are bounded at one hand-over per turn.

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `REFUSED` for a second hand-over in one turn, and `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a blank source.

parameters.name: source
parameters.doc: The program to run in place of this one, as Kotlin. It may not be blank.

functions.name: finish
functions.brief: End the session, reporting what was done in a sentence or two.
functions.detail:
It does not stop the program — whatever follows it still runs — so it belongs last, once the tools have confirmed the work is really done. A program that then fails cancels the ending, and the session gets another turn.

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `REFUSED` for a second ending in one turn.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: What was done, in a sentence or two.

functions.name: approve
functions.brief: Accept the work under review: it meets every completion criterion and stays in scope.
functions.detail:
This ends the session, and does not stop the program, so it belongs last — once the change has actually been read.

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `REFUSED` for a second verdict in one turn.

functions.name: requestChanges
functions.brief: Reject the work under review, listing every change that must be made before it can be accepted.
functions.detail:
Each item says what is wrong and what to change. This ends the session, and does not stop the program.

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` when the list is empty, and `REFUSED` for a second verdict in one turn.

parameters.name: items
parameters.doc: Every change that must be made before the work can be accepted, one per entry. The list may not be empty.

functions.name: wait
functions.brief: Register a wait on this issue, with its id already supplied.
functions.detail:
`gg.board.waitForIssue` for the common case where the created issue is in hand, written as a member so that the value carrying the id is what the call hangs off.

Returns: gg's acknowledgement that the wait is registered

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND` when the board no longer holds the issue.

functions.name: read
functions.brief: Read this hit's memory in full, with its slug already supplied.
functions.detail:
`gg.memories.readMemory` for the common case where the search result is in hand, written as a member so that the value carrying the slug is what the call hangs off.

Returns: the memory's contents

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND` when the memory has been deleted since the search.

functions.name: close
functions.brief: Close this view, with its selector already supplied.
functions.detail:
`gg.views.close` for the common case where the listed view is in hand, written as a member so that the value carrying the selector is what the call hangs off.

Returns: how many views were closed, which is `0` when this one has already gone

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an empty selector.

functions.name: send
functions.brief: Deliver a message to this child's inbox, with its id already supplied.
functions.detail:
`gg.delegation.sendMessage` for the common case where the handle is in hand, written as a member so that the value carrying the id is what the call hangs off.

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `CONFLICT` when this child has already returned.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to put in its inbox, which it reads at its next turn.

functions.name: source
functions.brief: The source of this program, with its turn already supplied.
functions.detail:
`gg.programs.get` for the common case where the summary is in hand, written as a member so that the value carrying the turn is what the call hangs off.

Returns: the source of the program that ran on that turn

Raises `gg.core.ToolError`: `NOT_FOUND` when the library has dropped that turn since the history was read.

types.name: Patch
types.declaration: sealed interface Patch<out T> { data class Replace(val value: T); data object Clear }
types.brief: One field of a revision that can be cleared as well as replaced.
types.detail:
Most of what `gg.tasks.updateTask` and `gg.board.updateIssue` take is two-way: naming a field replaces it and leaving it out keeps it. A description, and an issue's epic, are three-way — kept, replaced, or emptied — and `null` is already spoken for by the second of those, since leaving an argument out is passing `null` in this language. So the third state is a value rather than a sentinel, which is what a sealed type is for:

```
gg.tasks.updateTask("parse", description = gg.core.Patch.Replace("read the manifest first"))
gg.board.updateIssue("AUTH-1", epicId = gg.core.Patch.Clear)
```

members.brief: Empty the field, leaving it with nothing.

types.name: ToolErrorCode
types.declaration: enum class ToolErrorCode(val wireName: String) { INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, REFUSED, UNAVAILABLE, LIMIT_EXCEEDED, IO_ERROR, OTHER }
types.brief: Why a gg call failed — the `gg.core.ToolError.code` a catch site branches on.
types.detail: The set is gg's own and is closed. A code this SDK has no entry for reads as `OTHER` rather than failing the read, because a program handed an unclassified failure is better placed than a program handed a crash.

members.name: INVALID_ARGUMENT
members.brief: The arguments were malformed, ill-typed, or out of range.
members.detail: A path that is absolute or climbs out of the workspace is this, and so is an agent name the run does not declare.

members.name: NOT_FOUND
members.brief: The named thing does not exist.
members.detail: A file, skill, memory, task, epic, issue, subagent, stored program or documentation entry all report their absence this way.

members.name: CONFLICT
members.brief: Well-formed, and in conflict with the current state.
members.detail: An ambiguous edit, a dependency cycle, a duplicate id and a subagent that has already returned are each this.

members.name: REFUSED
members.brief: gg refused the call on a rule about the session's state.
members.detail: A compaction in flight that this call is not the one it asked for, a memory write while the memories are read-only, a second ending or hand-over in one turn, and a hook that blocked the call are each this. A ceiling that was reached is `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` instead.

members.name: UNAVAILABLE
members.brief: The call exists and this run's capability set does not offer it.

members.name: LIMIT_EXCEEDED
members.brief: A gg-side ceiling was reached.
members.detail: A shell timeout, a store cap, the delegation depth cap, one of the view caps a program spends, and the run's wall-clock budget are each this.

members.name: IO_ERROR
members.brief: The underlying input, output or process failed.

members.name: OTHER
members.brief: The failure was not classified.
members.detail: Reserved for outcomes raised outside a tool implementation; nothing in this SDK produces it.

members.name: wireName
members.brief: gg's own spelling of the code, which a run record and the tool-calling arm both report.

A picture is a different kind of thing from text, so it is a different arm rather than a string that happens to be binary — a program that treats an image as text is caught by the `when` instead of silently writing an empty string somewhere.
